id: SA-0317
title: "A PACKAGE raise's mark still counts toward the breaker; its own comment implied otherwise"
type: bug
priority: 3

forbidden:

budget_usd: 6

acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      The comment `run_task` carries beside its
      `mark_raised_in_package(exc)` call for a `READY_FOR_REVIEW` cell's
      `PackageError` (`saffron/task.py:900-901`) says the mark lets a
      batch "not count this as an ordinary abort." That is false:
      `saffron/batch.py`'s `_drive` runs `consecutive_aborts += 1`
      (`saffron/batch.py:312`) unconditionally, before it ever reads
      `marked = raised_in_package(exc)` (`saffron/batch.py:317`). The mark
      changes only which stop reason a batch closes on, forcing
      `INFRASTRUCTURE` (`saffron/batch.py:1024-1025`) — it does not exempt
      the raise from the breaker. One marked raise followed by one
      unmarked raise still trips the breaker at two, the same as two
      raises of either kind alone, and a third candidate queued behind
      them never runs.
    witness: tests/test_batch.py::test_a_marked_raise_shares_the_breakers_tally_with_an_ordinary_one
    wrong_versions:
      - "`_drive` reads `raised_in_package(exc)` before `consecutive_aborts += 1` and skips the increment when the raise is marked, so a marked raise followed by an unmarked one leaves the tally at one and the third candidate runs."
      - "`_promote_in_flight` resets `consecutive_aborts` to `0` whenever it closes a row `INFRASTRUCTURE` for a marked raise, so the breaker starts counting over from the next candidate."
      - "`_drive` increments `consecutive_aborts` only inside the `if marked:` branch, so an unmarked raise never advances the tally and a marked one followed by two unmarked ones never trips the breaker."
      - "`_drive` increments `consecutive_aborts` by `2` for an unmarked raise and leaves it unchanged for a marked one, so a marked raise followed by one unmarked raise reaches the same tally the comment's wrong half would predict only by coincidence, and a second unmarked raise overshoots it."
---

## Context

Finding against `SA-0316` (origin head `872215b4`): the comment
`run_task` writes just before `mark_raised_in_package(exc)`, for a
`READY_FOR_REVIEW` cell's `PackageError`, reads

> Marked so a batch can name `saffron package` as the fix, not count
> this as an ordinary abort (`b-066901`).

at `saffron/task.py:900-901`. "Not an ordinary stop reason" is true: the
mark forces `_promote_in_flight` to return `INFRASTRUCTURE`
(`saffron/batch.py:1024-1025`) whatever the loop's own reason was.
"Not counted as an abort" is false: `_drive`'s `except Exception` branch
runs `consecutive_aborts += 1` (`saffron/batch.py:312`) first, and only
after that reads `marked = raised_in_package(exc)` (`saffron/batch.py:317`).
The marked raise adds to the same tally an unmarked one would, with no
branch anywhere that skips the increment for it. `SA-0316`'s own spec
file gets this right in its own planning prose, naming criterion 2's
witness: "The marked raise still counts toward the breaker, as every
raise does (`saffron/batch.py:298`). Leave that count alone. Criterion
2 drives it."
(`.saffron/specs/SA-0316-a-batch-whose-package-raised-still-exits-0.md:361-362`
— prose in the spec file itself, not a docstring `_drive` or anything
else in `saffron/batch.py` carries), and
`tests/test_batch.py::test_a_batch_whose_package_raised_closes_infrastructure_whatever_it_stopped_on`'s
last block proves the two-marked-raises case. Neither proves the mixed
case — one marked raise, then one unmarked one — and only the comment
beside the mark itself states the two halves wrong enough to read as
one wrong claim: it is the comment a later editor of this exact branch
would read first.

## Problem

1. **Reword the comment.** Replace the two lines at
   `saffron/task.py:900-901` with wording that keeps both halves true:
   the mark routes a batch to `saffron package` and forces the row
   closed `INFRASTRUCTURE`, and `_drive`'s breaker still counts the
   raise toward `consecutive_aborts` like any other, because the
   increment at `saffron/batch.py:312` runs before anything there reads
   the mark. Cite `b-066901` as the existing comment does. Change
   nothing else on those lines: `mark_raised_in_package(exc)` and the
   bare `raise` after it keep their place and their behavior.
2. **Add a witness that pins the corrected reading.** In
   `tests/test_batch.py`, add a test that drives `run_batch` over three
   candidates whose first raises a marked `CellRuntimeError` (build it
   with the existing `_marked_runtime_error` helper) and whose second
   raises a plain, unmarked `CellRuntimeError`. Assert the returned
   reason is `INFRASTRUCTURE`, that only the first two candidates' ids
   appear in the runner's call order, that each of the first two specs
   gets a `raised` line, that only the first spec's id appears beside a
   `saffron package` command line, and that the second spec's id does
   not. This is the case the old comment's "not count this as an
   ordinary abort" reading would get backwards: a change that skipped
   the increment for the marked raise alone would let a third candidate
   run, since the tally would then read one, not two, when the second
   candidate's own unmarked raise is counted.

## Out of scope

- `saffron/batch.py` itself. Its `_drive`, `_promote_in_flight` and
  `_stop` already increment and promote correctly; this spec is
  forbidden from touching the file and needs no change to it.
- Every other comment and docstring `SA-0316` wrote. Its module
  docstring, and the docstrings on `_drive`, `wrapped`'s runner handler,
  `_is_layer`, `_promote_in_flight` and `_stop`, already describe a
  marked raise correctly; only the one comment cited above conflates
  the two halves.
- `tests/test_task.py` and `tests/test_cli.py`. Both are reachable
  paths for this follow-up, but the claim here is about `_drive`'s
  tally, not about `run_task`'s own marking (already witnessed by
  `tests/test_task.py::test_a_raise_that_escapes_run_task_from_package_is_marked_and_kept`)
  or about `saffron batch`'s exit code (already witnessed by
  `tests/test_cli.py::test_saffron_batch_exits_2_and_names_the_package_command_when_package_raised`).
  Neither needs a new witness for this finding.
- The exhausted-mode `except BaseException` branch two lines below
  (`saffron/task.py:909-911`). It carries no such comment and is not
  the one the finding names.

## Notes for the agent

The witness is a brand-new test, so it cannot declare `preserves: true`:
`saffron/intake.py`'s own `Criterion.preserves` docstring is explicit
that "a new test can never preserve: it did not pass at base," and
`saffron/gates/core/criteria.py::_judge` enforces exactly that — a
`preserves` criterion whose witness was not already green at `base_sha`
fails every time, and a test absent from `tests/test_batch.py` at base
cannot have been green there. This spec changes no runtime behavior —
only the comment, and `saffron/batch.py` is forbidden — so the claim is
about a tally `_drive` already gets right at base. The criterion is
declared the ordinary way instead: no `preserves`, a witness the suite
never collected at base (so `_judge`'s `witness-green-at-base` branch
cannot fire either, the same as any other brand-new test), and a
`wrong_versions` list naming the specific miscounts a later editor
*would* introduce into `saffron/batch.py` if they took the old comment's
wrong half at its word — the regression this follow-up's reworded
comment, and this witness, exist to keep out of that forbidden file,
not one this diff itself makes. Build the marked exception with
`_marked_runtime_error`, already defined in `tests/test_batch.py`
(it imports `mark_raised_in_package` inside its own body, so this
witness needs no module-scope import of anything `saffron.task` added).
